topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture on cancer therapy and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and chemotherapy resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine standard local and cytotoxic treatments for cancer alongside the toxicities and resistance mechanisms that limit their effectiveness.

topics.label: Targeting cancer cell vulnerabilities and synthetic lethality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how therapeutic strategies exploit specific intrinsic defects in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and impaired DNA repair.

topics.label: Kinase-targeted therapies and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the design of small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting driver oncogenes and analyze the genetic and pathway bypass mechanisms through which tumors develop resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapeutics and drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates are used to target specific cell surface markers on cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the role of immune surveillance and present therapeutic methods to mobilize or engineer T cells to eliminate tumor cells.

topics.label: Clinical challenges, historical progress, and future paradigms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overarching synthesis of therapeutic challenges, historical survival trends, emerging management strategies, and clinical trial dilemmas.
